items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 17, 2026
items.excerpt: 17 November 2026• Update: 17 November 2026 WASHINGTON Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start your Tuesday, including Germany's call on Israel to allow more aid to reach Gaza before winter, US President Donald Trump's indication of a possible meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his Asia trip, and Jordan's blocking of the Telegram messaging application as part of efforts to prevent the spread of “extremism and radicalization." German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul called on Israel to allow significantly more humanitarian aid to reach the Gaza Strip to prevent further deterioration as rainy and stormy winter months approach. Speaking to reporters ahead of an EU foreign ministers’ meeting in Brussels, Wadephul said the latest developments in the Middle East, especially the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, will be discussed by the ministers. "We are all concerned about the situation with the coming rainy and stormy winter months," he said. "The European message is clear: it is urgently necessary that significantly more humanitarian aid arrives in the Gaza Strip so that the humanitarian situation does not deteriorate further." Wadephul noted that he had raised the issue with colleagues last week at the G7 foreign ministers meeting and remains in constant contact with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar. - Trump says he 'may' meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during Asia trip US President Donald Trump said he "may" meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China during an upcoming diplomatic tour of Asia. "We could ... have a chance to accomplish a lot," Trump told reporters about his meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as he departed the White House, adding that a possible meeting with the North Korean leader depends on Kim and Xi. The US president said his itinerary will be focused largely on economic issues. Trump will arrive in the Philippine capital Manila on Tuesday for talks with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), a regional bloc, and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), a diplomatic partnership made up of the US, Australia, India and Japan. - Jordan blocks Telegram to counter attempts to spread ‘extremism, radicalization’ Jordan said it has blocked the Telegram messaging application as part of efforts to prevent the spread of “extremism and radicalization” through digital platforms, in the wake of last month’s church attack. In a statement carried by the official Petra news agency, the Public Security Directorate said the decision was aimed at strengthening digital security, protecting users and reducing risks associated with illegal activities on online platforms. The measure was intended to counter the use of digital platforms to facilitate cybercrime, threats, blackmail and the dissemination of illegal content, including attempts to promote “extremism and radicalization that could threaten national security,” it added. The directorate stressed that its actions are consistent with existing legislation and aimed at protecting public safety. ... - The first trilateral meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping will be the centerpiece of Putin's Nov. 18–19 visit to the Chinese city of Shenzhen, said Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov. ... - Five EU countries announce plans for 1st return hub outside Europe Five European countries and Rwanda announced that they are exploring the establishment of the first return hub outside Europe, aiming to reach an agreement and begin transferring rejected asylum seekers by 2027. Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands said in a joint statement published by Denmark's Immigration Ministry that the proposed facility would accommodate migrants without legal permission to remain in the participating EU countries and who are subject to enforceable return decisions. The initiative would allow transferred migrants to integrate into Rwandan society or voluntarily travel to their countries of origin or other countries where they can legally reside, with international support, according to the statement.

items.excerpt: Nov 17, 2026, 08:40:00 AM IST Orlando, Florida: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is facing the biggest test of his tenure so far. Just as the economic case for accelerating interest rate hikes is strengthening, political pressure to go easier has returned. Warsh officially replaced Jerome Powell as Fed chair on May 22. Most economic signs since then have indicated that tighter monetary policy is needed. Inflation has remained sticky and above target, largely due to persistently high energy prices caused by the Iran war. The AI investment boom has fueled record corporate earnings and stock prices, while the labor market and wider economy appear to be in good shape. The unemployment rate in October was just 4.1%, and annualized GDP growth in the third quarter accelerated to 3.4%. But the Fed has raised rates only once under Warsh's watch, a 25-basis-point increase in September. ... As several Fed officials have pointed out over the last two weeks, there is still a lot of "work to do" to get inflation down, as the October consumer price index print testified. Inflation was above forecasts for a third month, as high energy prices passed through the economy into "core" goods and services. So much so that a rare 50-bps hike next month is now on the table, and an additional 45 bps of tightening by the end of next year has been added to the rate futures curve. items.title: Hammack Favors Gradual Fed Hikes, Cites Firms’ Growing Willingness to Raise Prices | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented from the Fed’s Oct. 28 decision to hold rates, favoring a quarter-point increase as she raised concerns about firms passing price rises to customers. In a Nov. 16 interview with Bloomberg Television, Hammack said businesses appeared increasingly inclined to shift higher prices to customers. She reiterated her preference for a gradual pace of interest-rate moves. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept its target range at 3.75% to 4.00%. The vote was 10-2; Fed Governor Lisa D. Cook also dissented, with both her and Hammack favoring a 0.25-percentage-point increase. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported that the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October from the previous month, following a 0.6% increase in September. The index excluding food and energy advanced 0.3% in October, matching its monthly gains in August and September. The October release lacks the usual year-over-year changes for affected series because the BLS did not collect October 2025 data during a lapse in appropriations. The CPI is separate from the personal consumption expenditures price index, whose annual change the Fed uses to assess its longer-run 2% inflation goal.

items.title: Chicago Fed President: Persistent High Inflation Could Be ‘Painful to Try to Get Rid Of’
items.excerpt: Inflation has been above the Federal Reserve Bank’s target since February 2021. Those five and a half years have seen periods of progress and setbacks. But the direction inflation is headed now — with high prices expanding beyond temporary shocks from tariffs and the Iran war — is raising eyebrows. “At this moment, we’ve got to be very cognizant that we’re dancing on the edge of something that’s hard and potentially painful to get rid of,” said Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago. ... The consumer price index for all items rose 0.4% in one month, according to data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) last week. Last year’s government shutdown prevented the BLS from comparing prices to October 2025. But estimates place the annual inflation rate near 4%, double the Fed’s target. When higher-than-desired inflation sticks around that long, “it’s even more painful to try to get rid of,” Goolsbee said. “If people start taking for granted that inflation is going to be this high next year, the year after, et cetera, then they start factoring it into their decisions.” If the expectation of sustained inflation hangs over businesses’ decisions on topics like wage negotiations and cost planning, the central bank can have a harder time bringing inflation down. ... Goolsbee pointed to “negative shocks,” including tariffs and high prices of oil, that knocked prices off of this path. But he sees a different trend emerging now, where services not directly connected to these shocks are starting to see inflation. Goolsbee gave health insurance as an example of a service that’s seeing price spikes. “Health insurance inflation is not coming from tariffs, is not coming from oil prices, is not coming from any of the things that you could envision turning on a dime,” Goolsbee said. “Historically, things like health insurance, when they get ramped up they stay up and they keep rising.”

items.title: Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid Says Inflation Remains Too High | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: inflation remained above the Federal Reserve’s 2% objective, and Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City President Jeff Schmid said Sunday that reducing price growth had become more difficult since August. He made the remarks at the National Credit Union Management Association 2026 Conference in Kohala Coast, Hawai’i. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.6% from a year earlier in September, the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported. The index excluding food and energy increased 3.1% over the same period. For the month, the overall index rose 0.5% and the core measure gained 0.3%. Schmid cited a 5.7% annualized rise in consumer price index (CPI) prices over the three months through October. That is a three-month pace, not a year-over-year rate. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said October CPI rose 0.4% from the previous month, seasonally adjusted. It did not publish a 12-month rate because October 2025 comparison data were unavailable after a lapse in federal appropriations. Schmid described the labor market as largely balanced, with wage growth around 3% and about one available job for each job seeker. He pointed to higher oil costs, tariffs, demand tied to artificial intelligence infrastructure and rising health care expenses as sources of price pressure. Employer health-benefit costs, he said, had risen more than 6% over the past year, their fastest pace in more than 20 years.

items.title: US consumer prices increase strongly for third straight month - Business Recorder
items.excerpt: Published November 15, 2026 Updated November 15, 2026 02:35am By Reuters WASHINGTON: US consumer prices increased more than expected in October, driven by higher costs for food and accommodation, leaving the Federal Reserve on course to raise interest rates next month. The Consumer Price Index report from the Labor Department on Tuesday also showed a strong buildup of underlying inflation pressures for the third straight month. The Labor Department’s Bureau of Labour Statistics did not publish year-over-year inflation readings because last year’s federal government shutdown prevented the collection of consumer price data in October 2025, leaving no comparison base. Annual consumer inflation jumped 3.7 percent in September. Inflation is running well above the US central bank’s 2 percent target. The US-Israeli war with Iran has boosted oil prices, combining with the import tariffs implemented by the Trump administration last year to lift the cost of living. High inflation contributed to the heavy losses suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections last week. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Tuesday that the US central bank should raise rates next month, adding that “a stronger policy move may be needed.” Waller also raised the prospect of a 50 basis point hike if core consumer prices, excluding food and energy, increased 0.3 percent or more from September, which they did. “Consumers’ inflation nightmare continues with no relief in sight,” said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. “Fed officials are going to need to bring a bigger hose if they have any hope of putting the inflation fire out.” The CPI increased 0.4 percent last month after advancing 0.6 percent in September. It was the third consecutive month of CPI gains of 0.4 percent or more. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the CPI climbing 0.3 percent over the month. Shelter, which includes rents, hotel and motel rooms, accounted for more than 30 percent of the increase in the CPI last month. Shelter costs rose 0.3 percent after climbing 0.4 percent in September. Food prices surged 0.5 percent after barely rising in the prior three months. Grocery store prices rebounded 0.4 percent, boosted by a 0.9 percent jump in the cost of beef. Egg prices rose 0.6 percent while fruits and vegetables were 0.6 percent more expensive. Prices for dairy and related products rose 0.6 percent. The cost of snacks surged 1.0 percent. Higher prices at the supermarket could be a reflection of more expensive diesel fuel. The cost of eating out also increased last month, with prices of food away from home surging 0.5 percent after rising 0.2 percent in September. The cost of full service meals increased 0.7 percent. Gasoline prices climbed 1.0 percent after soaring 9.1 percent. Though diesel prices have come down from record highs, they rose 2.7 percent last month after increasing 11.9 percent in September. STRONG CORE INFLATION Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI increased 0.3 percent in October, advancing by the same margin for three months in a row. The so-called core CPI was forecast to have climbed 0.2 percent in October. Core CPI inflation increased 2.6 percent year-over-year in September. It was last month driven by a 0.3 percent rise in owners’ equivalent rent, a measure of the amount homeowners would pay to rent or would earn from renting their property. Prices for hotel and motel rooms rose 0.6 percent. Airline fares rose 0.4 percent. The cost of recreation increased 0.8 percent, while motor vehicle insurance advanced 0.7 percent. Household furnishings and supplies prices rebounded 0.7 percent, suggesting that some pass-through from tariffs remained. There were also increases in the prices of new vehicles, medication and recreation goods.

President Donald Trump’s net approval rating improved 3 percentage points over the past week, with 46% approving and 51% disapproving in our latest tracker update. That improvement comes as the federal government’s Oct. 1 shutdown remains our most salient story for the third week in a row. It’s just the latest indication that, as we get into more below, the impasse on Capitol Hill may be full of sound and fury, but signifies nothing for the average voter. ... Shutdown Trump is set to host Senate Republicans for lunch at the White House today “to celebrate their unity in the government shutdown fight and for passing nominees,” according to Politico, which noted that the party’s push for a Nov. 21 funding extension may need to change as Washington gets closer to the expiration date. Some conservatives are said to be pushing for a continuing resolution that would run until March or even next October, though the idea irks Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine). Perhaps most notably: NOTUS reports that some Republican senators — even Collins herself — are beginning to entertain the idea of employing the nuclear option to pass a continuing resolution with a simple majority. On the Obamacare front, Politico also reports that Republicans are ramping up talks with the White House on what kind of premium tax credit expansion the party could support once the government is reopened. The party is said to be considering a year-end health care policy package with a two-year extension of scaled-back ACA subsidies though it’s uncertain how that would be received in the House. Nominees The New York Times reports that Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) is among at least four Republican senators who have come out in opposition to Trump’s nomination of Paul Ingrassia to lead the Office of Special Counsel following a Politico report documenting a series of racist text messages. That’s enough Republicans to kill Ingrassia’s nomination even before his planned testimony to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Thursday. ... House Democratic leaders in Washington have devised a new congressional boundary map for Illinois that would target Republican Rep. Darin LaHood, aiming to reduce the state’s GOP-leaning districts to two, Punchbowl News reports on the party’s response to GOP gerrymandering efforts. Legislators will be in a veto session next week, but will have to move fast ahead of Illinois' pending filing deadline or move next year’s primary date.

items.excerpt: November 16, 2026 | 7:19 pm ## Ben&Ben, Take That team up for new song PINOY folk-pop band Ben&Ben has collaborated with legendary British pop group Take That for the song “Glow.” The result of months of back-and-forth work, mostly done online, the song was unveiled on Nov. 14 as Ben&Ben frontmen Miguel Benjamin and Paolo Benjamin joined the Take That trio on stage at the iconic The London Palladium, where they sang the song for the first time. “Glow” is part of the deluxe edition of Take That’s 10 th studio album Dreamers, which will be released on Nov. 20. For the British pop group, the Philippines is “one of its most important markets,” which led to the collaboration with Ben&Ben who displayed similarities in their song themes and musical styles. This is the first time that Take That has partnered with Filipino artists. ... ## IV OF SPADES drops new single, announces new album FOLLOWING a successful year in music, IV OF SPADES has dropped a new alt-pop track “Susundan,” out now via Sony Music Entertainment. It will be part of their upcoming third studio album, TROPICAL DREAM, which is slated for release on Dec. 9. A sincere but desperate take on romantic longing, the track explores the experience of pursuing someone who remains frustratingly out of reach. Blending retro sensibilities with ’90s alt rock, it was written by Blaster Silonga and composed by IV OF SPADES. It is out now on all digital music platforms worldwide.

items.title: Reuters Entertainment News Summary | International
items.excerpt: # Reuters Entertainment News Summary Reuters | Updated: 17-11-2026 10:27 IST | Created: 17-11-2026 10:27 IST Following is a summary of current entertainment news briefs. Raye and Rosalia lead nominations for music's Grammy Awards British ​singer Raye, the artist behind the genre-mixing hit that asks "Where Is ​My Husband!," landed at the top of the list of ‌Grammy ​Award nominees on Monday, ahead of Spanish musician Rosalia and "Choosin' Texas" artist Ella Langley. Raye earned 11 Grammy nominations including nods for song and record of the year for "Husband," and for album of the year for "This Music May Contain Hope." ‌Rosalia racked up nine nominations, days after she dominated the Latin Grammys with her album "Lux." British actor Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond British actor Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday, taking on one of cinema's most coveted roles. The Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his ‌charm, his tailored tuxedos and a fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. Kids' Choice Awards honor Chris Pratt, ‌BTS The Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards on Saturday honored Chris Pratt with the "King of Comedy" title, while South Korean boy band BTS took home favorite album for "ARIRANG" and "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" won favorite movie. BTS also secured the award for favorite music group, their fifth time in this category, as well as a win for favorite song with "Swim". Tom Holland and Zendaya gained the best male and female ⁠actor awards for ​their roles in "Spider-Man: Brand New Day". UK authorities ⁠investigating after Russell Brand's message from prison British authorities are investigating whether Russell Brand, the comedian found guilty of rape, has broken rules which ban prisoners from making statements that can cause distress to victims, ⁠the Prime Minister's spokesperson said on Monday. Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spokesperson was asked about comments made by Brand's wife Laura on a YouTube podcast, during which she read out ​a statement from him saying he was innocent. Hollywood salutes Glenn Close and Ridley Scott with honorary Oscars Hollywood's big-screen stars celebrated the careers of actor Glenn ⁠Close and director Ridley Scott on Sunday at the annual Governors Awards, one of the first red-carpet events of the movie awards season. The pair were among five film industry heavyweights bestowed with honorary Oscars ⁠at ​a gala attended by A-list actors from Tom Cruise to power couple Zendaya and Tom Holland. French actor Gerard Depardieu withdraws his sexual assault appeal, apologises to victims French actor Gérard Depardieu on Monday withdrew his appeal against a 2025 conviction for sexual assault, accepting his guilt and apologising to his victims. In a statement, Depardieu said ⁠he had often used "vulgar, sexually suggestive humour" on set and now realized "there is a line between cheekiness and offence". After Brand and Walliams, UK entertainment industry under pressure to ⁠clean up its act The rape conviction ⁠of Russell Brand and sexual misconduct accusations against David Walliams have reignited calls for tighter safeguards in Britain's entertainment industry and a review of legal tools used by celebrities to silence those who try to call out bad behaviour. Brand, once one ‌of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters, ‌was jailed for 10-1/2 years last week after he was found guilty of rape ​and sexual assault around two decades ago.

items.title: New Music Friday: Britney Spears, Olivia Rodrigo and JENNIE Lead Releases
items.excerpt: November 17, 2026 3 min read By Emily Parker New Music Friday has arrived with a packed slate of releases led by Britney Spears, Olivia Rodrigo and JENNIE, alongside new projects from Kings of Leon, Good Charlotte and others. The week also brings major tour and awards news. ## Britney Spears Marks 25 Years Britney Spears has released a 25th Anniversary Edition of her album Britney. ## Olivia Rodrigo Offers a Holiday Track Olivia Rodrigo has shared a new song titled “take me home (4 christmas).” ## JENNIE Debuts Animated Film Song JENNIE has released “Someone To Hold,” her first song for an animated film. Written and produced by Justin Tranter, the track will play over the end credits of Netflix’s upcoming animated film Steps. It will also appear on the Steps (Soundtrack from the Netflix Film), due November 20. ## Kings of Leon Return With O My Beloved Kings of Leon have released O My Beloved. ## Good Charlotte Expand Greetings From California Good Charlotte have shared Greetings From California (Deluxe). ## More New Releases Dove Cameron has released FINAL GIRL, while Billy Ray Cyrus offers THE HILL (Deluxe). GloRilla and Sexyy Red team up on “Jiggly Bow Bow,” and Thomas Rhett has shared “Be There In A Minute.” Additional releases include Florence + The Machine’s Everybody Scream Tour Live, Lil Baby’s FRESH, Coi Leray’s “Spin Back,” XG’s “DEPENDS,” Jessie Reyez’s A LITTLE VENGEANCE (is more human than no vengeance at al), TWS’s TO US, Shenseea’s Catalyst, Hudson Westbrook’s Made You Look, Blu DeTiger’s N.Y. Baby, Kingston Rossdale’s Louise Street, Dylan Marlowe’s self-titled album, Sophia James’s Sleepwalking at 65 MPH and Jesse Jo Stark’s MUSE. ## The Weeknd Sets Tour Record The Weeknd’s After Hours Til Dawn Tour has become the highest-grossing tour by a male artist in history, surpassing $1.3 billion. The tour concluded with a final performance at TM Stadium National in Kuala Lumpur. Across 176 shows in 67 cities, 30 countries and five continents, the run sold more than 9 million tickets and grossed over $1.3 billion USD. The Weeknd has donated $8.5 million to the XO Humanitarian Fund and Global Citizen to support global hunger relief and access to quality education for children worldwide. ## Awards News The CMA has announced the first performers for The 60th Annual CMA Awards: Cody Johnson, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley, Tim McGraw, Kacey Musgraves, The Red Clay Strays, Zach Top and Tucker Wetmore. A special tribute to Dolly Parton is also planned. Hosted by Lainey Wilson, the awards will air live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on November 18 on ABC and Disney+, and stream the next day on Hulu. The Latin Recording Academy has added performers for the 27th Annual Latin GRAMMY Awards, including Baby Ranks, Bad Gyal, Bizarrap, Miguel Colón, Divino, DJ Premier, Diljit Dosanjh, Grupo Niche, Jay Wheeler, KAROL G, Lil Supa, Luis Enrique, Nathy Peluso and Ángel “Cucco” Peña. The awards will air live from the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas on Univision, UNIMÁS and Galavisión, and stream on VIX. ## Songwriter Honored Jenna Andrews received Songwriter of the Year in the Non-Performer category at the 2026 SOCAN Awards, held at Toronto’s REBEL nightclub. She was recognized for “Free” and “What It Sounds Like” from the K-Pop Demon Hunters soundtrack.
